info.title: Huxley API
info.description: Huxley platform API. See https://docs.usehuxley.com for conventions.

get.summary: Approvals waiting for you, then the ones you decided in the last 30 days.
One approval: for its approvers, and anyone who can read the run.

post.summary:
Approves or rejects. The first decision counts; the workflow continues
with it as the step's output.

delete.summary: Removes a file from its record.

get.summary:
Downloads a file. Always served as a download (never shown inline), with
only a few content types passed through, so an uploaded page or script
can't run in the app's origin.
Lists audit events, newest first.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only actions starting with this prefix, e.g. `auth.` or `org.created`.

get.summary:
Downloads the audit log, oldest first, as JSON lines or CSV. Streams in
batches, so large logs don't need to fit in memory. Each row carries its
chain hashes. The export itself is audited.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only actions starting with this prefix.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Events at or after this time (RFC 3339).

post.summary: Emails the signed-in user a link to verify their address.
Verifies an address with the emailed link. No session needed.

Signs in with email and password. Sets the session cookie, or asks for a
second factor if the user has one.

200.description: Signed in (session cookie set), or a second factor is required

401.description: Wrong email or password, or the account is disabled or locked

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

post.summary:
Completes sign-in with a second factor. Send exactly one of `code` or
`recoveryCode`.

401.description: Wrong code, or the challenge expired or ran out of attempts

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

post.summary:
Options for answering an MFA challenge with a passkey. Finish with
`POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa` and a `passkey` answer.

Signs in with a passkey alone. A passkey verifies the user on the device,
so no second factor is asked for.

401.description: The passkey could not be verified

post.summary: Options for passwordless sign-in with a passkey.
Signs out the current session and clears the cookie.

get.summary: The signed-in user.
Sign-in methods offered by this server.
The signed-in user's MFA setup.

post.summary: Replaces the recovery codes. The old ones stop working.

Starts setting up an authenticator app. Returns the secret to scan; the
app isn't required at sign-in until `/totp/confirm` succeeds.

Finishes authenticator setup with a code from the app. Returns recovery
codes (shown once) and signs out the user's other sessions.
Turns off the authenticator app and deletes recovery codes.

Completes single sign-on with the provider's `code` and `state`. Sets the
session cookie.

get.summary: Enabled sign-in options, for the sign-in page.

post.summary:
Starts single sign-on. The provider redirects back to
`{auth.public_url}/login/oidc/callback` with `code` and `state`.

get.summary: The signed-in user's passkeys.

post.summary: Finishes adding a passkey with the browser's answer.

422.description: Invalid answer, name, or expired request

post.summary: Starts adding a passkey (re-checks the password).

delete.summary:
Removes a passkey. Removing the last second factor also deletes the
recovery codes.

post.summary: Changes the signed-in user's password. Signs out all their other sessions.

204.description: Password changed; other sessions signed out

422.description: Current password wrong or new password too weak

post.summary:
Emails a password reset link if the address belongs to an account with a
password. Responds the same way whether or not it does.

202.description: If the account exists and can reset, a link is on its way

post.summary:
Sets a new password with a reset or invitation link. Signs out every
session; sign in again afterwards.

get.summary: The signed-in user's active sessions.

delete.summary: Revokes one of the signed-in user's sessions, e.g. a lost device.

404.description: No such session for this user

get.summary: Your API tokens. Needs a signed-in session (not a token).

post.summary:
Creates a personal access token that acts as you, narrowed to `scopes`.
It must expire within a year. Needs a signed-in session (not a token).

delete.summary: Revokes one of your API tokens.

get.summary: Connections the caller can see.

post.summary:
Creates a connection. The integration must belong to the connection's
organization or one above it.

Finishes a sign-in the caller started: exchanges the provider's code
for tokens. Each `state` works once, for ten minutes, for the person
who started it.

put.summary: Changes a connection. Secret fields left out keep their value.

post.summary:
Starts signing in a connection that uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code.
The redirect URI is always the app's own callback, never the caller's
choice.

get.summary: Custom field definitions for a record type.

patch.summary:
Changes a field's label, help, options, required flag, scope, or order.
Its key and type can't change.

post.summary: Archives (hides) or restores a field. Stored values are kept.

get.summary: A record's attachments, newest first.

post.summary: Uploads a file (multipart field `file`) to a record.

get.summary: The custom fields that apply to a record, with values.

patch.summary: Sets custom field values on a record.

get.summary: Record types that support custom fields and tags.
Forms you can fill in or manage.

put.summary: Replaces a form's definition (its key stays).

post.summary: Archives a form: it can't be submitted until restored.

get.summary:
A field's choices, looked up through its `options_from` action for the
organization the form is being filled in for.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization it's being filled in for (default: the form's).

post.summary:
A public link: anyone with it can fill the form in for one
organization, without signing in. Their runs act as each workflow's
run-as account. Forms that look choices up can't have one.
Stops a public link working at once.

get.summary: The latest submissions, for people who manage the form.

post.summary:
Submits answers. Starts the published workflows with a form trigger
for this form, as you; answers that don't fit are a 422 per field.

get.summary: Integrations the caller can view.

post.summary:
Imports a spec as a new integration. Problems the importer worked
around are returned as `warnings`; an unusable spec is a 422 on `spec`.

get.summary:
The actions workflows in an organization can call: those of the
nearest integration with each key, in the organization or above. For
the workflow editor's action picker.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization a workflow belongs to.

get.summary: The built-in integrations that can be added.

post.summary: Adds a built-in integration to an organization, under its catalog key.

get.summary: An integration with its current definition.

put.summary:
Makes an earlier imported version current again (a rollback), or a
later one after rolling back.

Replaces the integration's overlay: your names, descriptions and groups
for its actions, and which are hidden. Kept across new versions.

post.summary:
What importing a newer spec would change, and whether any of it can
break workflows or connections. Nothing is saved.

put.summary:
Imports a newer spec as the integration's next version, and makes it
current. Preview it first to see what changes.

get.summary: Every imported version, newest first.

Workflow jobs that failed repeatedly and were set aside (dead letters).
A dead step job has already failed its step: resume the run instead.

post.summary: Puts a dead job back in the queue with fresh attempts.

get.summary: Every feature module and whether it's enabled and active.

put.summary:
Turns a feature module on or off for the instance. Data is kept when a
module is turned off.

409.description: Missing dependencies, or enabled modules depend on it

get.summary: Your notifications, newest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.

get.summary: Your channel choices for each kind of notification.

put.summary: Chooses the channels for one kind. Security notices can't be changed.

get.summary:
Server-Sent Events: an `unread` event with your unread count when the
stream opens and whenever a notification arrives. Closes after ten minutes
(reconnect to continue).
Organizations the caller can see, ordered as a tree (parents before children).

post.summary: Creates a sub-organization.

409.description: Name already used by a sibling

post.summary: Archives an organization with no active sub-organizations.

get.summary:
Every module's state at an organization, including narrowing by a
provider org on its chain.

put.summary:
Turns a module off for a provider organization (below the root) and its
sub-organizations, or back on. Only narrows what the instance has on.

post.summary:
Moves an organization and its subtree under a new parent. Requires
`org:move` on the organization and `org:create` on the new parent.

get.summary:
Every setting at an organization: the effective value, where it comes
from (this org, an ancestor, or the default), and any ancestor lock.

put.summary: Sets a value at this organization, for it and its sub-organizations.

delete.summary: Removes this organization's value, so it inherits again.

get.summary:
The variables in effect at an organization: its own and inherited ones.
Secret values are never returned.

put.summary: Sets a variable at an organization (for it and those below).

delete.summary: Removes a variable from an organization; it inherits again.

get.summary: The packs installed in an organization.

post.summary:
Uploads a `.hxpack` (the request body) and returns what installing it in
`orgId` would do. Nothing is installed yet.

get.summary: What installing an uploaded pack in `orgId` would do.

post.summary:
Installs (or upgrades) an uploaded pack in an organization. Workflows
arrive as drafts, to review and publish.

get.summary: Every permission Huxley checks.

post.summary: Grants a role to a user at an organization.

get.summary: Roles that can be assigned.

post.summary:
Creates a custom role. It may only contain permissions you hold
instance-wide; only owners can create a role with `*`.

403.description: Missing role:manage, or a permission you don't hold

put.summary:
Replaces a custom role's name, description, and permissions. Holders get
the change at their next request.

delete.summary: Deletes a custom role that nobody holds.

get.summary: Every runner, active ones first.

post.summary: A runner enrols: the token (used once) proves who sent it. No session.
A single-use token for a new runner to enrol with (valid 24 hours).

Registers a runner whose certificate comes from your own CA
(`runners.client_ca_file`); its certificate's common name is `name`.
Stops a runner at once: the gateway refuses it from its next call.

get.summary: Runs the caller can view, newest first.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Runs older than this run id (for paging).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 200).

get.summary: A run with every step that has started.

post.summary: Asks a run to stop. Steps in flight finish; nothing new starts.

Resumes a failed run from the step that failed: steps that succeeded
aren't run again.

get.summary: A script step attempt's task: where it ran, how it ended, its logs.

A step attempt's full input or output. Values over the spill threshold
are kept in object storage, and the run shows a `$spilled` marker in
their place; this returns the value itself either way.

Server-Sent Events: a `run` event with the run (as `GET /runs/{id}`
returns it) when the stream opens and after each change, at most four a
second. Ends once the run has finished, or after ten minutes (reconnect
to continue).
Scripts you can see.
A script with its current version.
Every version, newest first.

post.summary:
Saves the next version and makes it current. With `baseVersion`, a
script changed meanwhile is a 409.

get.summary: One version's source and parameters.
Who must have a second factor.

put.summary:
Requires (or stops requiring) a second factor for users who can reach an
organization. On the root organization, that's every user.

Requires (or stops requiring) a second factor for holders of a role.
Holders without one can only set one up until they do.

get.summary: Configured identity providers.

post.summary: Adds an identity provider.

get.summary: One provider with its role mappings.

put.summary: Replaces a provider's settings. Omit `clientSecret` to keep the stored one.

delete.summary:
Deletes a provider, the identities linked to it, and the roles its
mappings granted. Users are kept.

put.summary:
Replaces a provider's claim → role mappings. Applied at each user's next
sign-in. The Owner role can't be mapped.

get.summary: Service accounts: non-human identities for integrations and scripts.

post.summary:
Creates a service account. Grant it roles with `POST /role-assignments`,
then create tokens for it.

patch.summary: Renames, describes, disables, or re-enables a service account.

post.summary: Creates a token for a service account. It may be non-expiring.

delete.summary: Deletes a tag and removes it from every record.

get.summary: Teams. Anyone who can view users can view teams.
The teams a user belongs to.
A team with its members and role assignments.

delete.summary: Deletes a team and the roles it held. Members keep their own roles.

put.summary: Adds a user to a team (idempotent). They get the team's roles at once.

delete.summary: Removes a user from a team. They lose the team's roles at once.

get.summary:
The built-in templates, and (with `orgId`) those saved at that
organization and above it.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Also list the templates saved at this organization and above it.

delete.summary: Deletes one of your organization's templates.

post.summary: Creates the template's form (if any) and a draft workflow from it.

get.summary: Lists users (people and service accounts; filter with `kind`).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.

post.summary: Creates a local user. The new user has no roles until one is assigned.

patch.summary: Edits a user's name or status.

get.summary: A user's role assignments that the caller can see.

What a user may do at an organization, and why: each permission with the
grants (role, org, team) that give it.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization to evaluate at. Defaults to the root.

delete.summary:
Removes a user's second factors (authenticator app and recovery codes) and
signs them out everywhere, for when they've lost access to both. Only an
owner can reset an owner's MFA.

204.description: MFA removed; the user signs in with a password and can set it up again

get.summary: Workflows the caller can view.

post.summary: Creates a workflow from a draft document.

409.description: Key already used in the org

post.summary: Checks a document without saving it.
Archives a workflow: it can't be edited or run until restored.

put.summary: Saves the draft. Fails with 409 if someone else saved since `revision`.

post.summary:
Evaluates an expression against a run of the workflow (the latest by
default), as a top-level step of it would see it. Secret values stay
redacted, and `secrets.*` isn't available.
Publishes the draft as a new version. 422 lists its problems if it has any.

put.summary:
Sets the service account that runs started by a schedule, webhook or
event act as. Needs `workflow:publish` on the workflow and
`service_account:manage`: whoever hands out an account's identity could
already act as it.

post.summary:
Starts a manual run: of the latest published version, or a test run of
the draft.

Saves the workflow's draft as a template of its organization, offered
there and below. If a form starts it, the form comes along, and each
use of the template gets its own copy.

get.summary: The published version's triggers: webhook paths and schedule times.
Liveness probe.
The form a public link opens.

post.summary: Submits answers through a public link.

get.summary: Readiness probe. Checks the database.

auth.description:
Auth scheme keys any one of which works; empty means none is needed
(or the spec doesn't say).

hidden.description: Hidden by the integration's overlay: not offered, still callable.

inputSchema.description: One object schema: each parameter by name, plus `body`.

key.description:
Unique in the definition: the `operationId` made safe, or
`<method>_<path>` when there is none.

outputSchema.description: The JSON schema of the first successful response, if it has one.

oneOf.description: How it pages through results (from the overlay).

ActionOption.description: An action a workflow in some organization can call: for pickers.

hidden.description: Not offered when picking actions (still callable).

oneOf.description: How the action pages through results, for `all_pages`.

AffectedWorkflow.description: A published workflow an update would break.

hint.description: The start of the token, to tell tokens apart.

ApprovalView.description: An approval as approvers see it.

workflowName.description: The workflow's name, if the run is of a saved workflow.

teamId.description: Set for an assignment to a team.

userId.description: Set for an assignment to a user.

oneOf.description: A key sent in a header, query parameter or cookie.

AuthMethodsView.description: Sign-in methods this server offers, for the sign-in page.

key.description: The spec's name for it (the `securitySchemes` key).

BindingKind.description: What a binding holds, which decides how it's checked and inserted.

cancelled.description: False if the run had already finished.

CatalogEntry.description: A built-in integration as the catalog shows it.

CeremonyView.description: The first half of a WebAuthn ceremony.

ceremony.description: Send back with the browser's answer.

Change.description: One difference, and whether it can break workflows or connections.

code.description: A current six-digit code from the app.

ConnectionInput.description: What a connection is made from (or changed to).

authScheme.description: One of the integration's auth scheme keys; none for open APIs.

key.description: Defaults to one made from the name.

secrets.description: Secret values. On update, fields left out keep their value.

ConnectionView.description: A connection as shown: settings, and which secrets are set.

secretFields.description: Names of the secret fields that have a value.

shared.description: Usable by the organizations below this one.

inherit.description: Also apply to every sub-organization (default true).

teamId.description: Grant to this team; its members receive the role.

userId.description: Grant to this user. Send exactly one of `userId` or `teamId`.

orgId.description:
The organization submissions are for: the form's (default) or one
below it.

expiresInDays.description: 1 to 366 for people. Omit (service accounts only) for no expiry.

scopes.description:
Permission keys the token may use, or `["*"]` for everything its
owner may do. Scopes only narrow the owner's roles.

invite.description:
Email the user an invitation to choose their own password instead.
Needs email to be configured.

password.description:
Initial password. If omitted (and not inviting), one is generated and
returned once.

generatedPassword.description: Present only when Huxley generated the password. Shown once.

document.description:
An HWF document. It may be incomplete, but needs `metadata.key` and
`metadata.name`.

token.description: Shown once: the link is `<web app>/f/<token>`.

tokenSecret.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Shown only now.

DeadJob.description: A job that used up its attempts.

comment.description: Shown on the run, at most 2000 characters.

Definition.description: An API, as Huxley uses it.

breaking.description: True if any change can break something already using the integration.

connection.description: Auth and server changes, which matter to connections.

removed.description:
Actions that are gone (renamed ones are listed under `renamed`, and
keep working under their old key).

DiagnosticView.description: A problem with a workflow document, and where it is.

csrPem.description: PEM certificate signing request for the runner's own key.

caPem.description: The CA to trust for the gateway.

token.description: Shown once: the runner uses it with `huxley runner enroll`.

EntityType.description: An entity type that supports custom fields and tags.

expression.description: The expression, as written in the workflow, e.g. `"{{ steps.a.output.id }}"`.

runId.description: A run of this workflow to evaluate against. Default: the latest.

FieldChanges.description:
Changes to a field. The key and type never change (stored values depend
on them).

clearScope.description: Apply the field to every org again (removes the scope).

scopeOrgId.description: Limit the field to this org's subtree.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the invalid field, e.g. `/name`.

FieldValue.description: A field that applies to an entity, with its value (null when unset).

name.description: A label to tell passkeys apart, e.g. "Work laptop".

FormInput.description: A form's definition, to create or replace it.

GrantSource.description: One grant that gives a permission.

teamName.description: Set when the grant comes through a team.

key.description: Defaults to one made from the spec's title.

spec.description: The OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0 document, as JSON or YAML text.

version.description: The version you reviewed: installing fails if the upload isn't it.

items.description: What was created or updated, by kind then key.

definition.description: The current version, with the overlay applied.

overlay.description: Your edits to its actions, kept across versions.

warnings.description: What the importer skipped or guessed in the current version.

IntegrationDetail.description: An integration with its current definition.

apiVersion.description: The API's own version, from the spec.

LinkView.description: A public link as its managers see it (never the token).

LocalSetting.description: A value set at the org itself.

code.description: A six-digit code from the authenticator app.

recoveryCode.description: One of the user's recovery codes. Each works once.

oneOf.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

next.description: Where to go next (single sign-on remembers it across the redirect).

oneOf.description: The password was right; finish with `POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa`.

challenge.description: Pass to `/login/mfa`. Valid for a few minutes and a few attempts.

LoginResponse.description: The result of a sign-in step.

activeModules.description: Feature modules that are enabled and released.

grantedPermissions.description:
Permissions granted at any organization. For deciding what to show;
the API enforces permissions on every request regardless.

isOwner.description: Holds the Owner role at the root organization.

mfaSetupRequired.description:
Policy requires a second factor and the user has none. Until they add
one, every API call except profile and MFA setup returns
`403 mfa-setup-required`.

MeView.description: The signed-in user plus permission hints for the UI.

MfaMethodView.description: Second-factor methods offered for a challenge.

MfaPolicy.description: The whole MFA policy at a glance.

everyone.description: Every user must have a second factor (set on the root organization).

orgs.description: Organizations whose users must have a second factor.

roleIds.description: Roles whose holders must have a second factor.

totpEnabled.description: An authenticator app is set up and required at sign-in.

MfaTrust.description: When an SSO sign-in counts as multi-factor for the MFA policy.

phase.description: Implementation-plan phase in which the module ships.

released.description: Whether this version of Huxley includes the module.

requires.description: Modules that must be enabled for this one to work.

active.description: Enabled and released: the module is running.

ModuleState.description: A module's state for the instance.

NewField.description: Settings for a new field. `key` is optional (derived from the label).

parameters.description: JSON Schema (an object) of its parameters; default: none.

NewVersion.description: The next version of a script.

baseVersion.description:
The version this edit started from: if the script has moved on
since, nothing is saved (409).

OrgKind.description:
`provider`: the owning company, an MSP brand, or a division. `client`: a
customer of a provider, or a site/sub-org of one.

active.description: Running here: enabled here and released.

enabledHere.description: On for this organization (instance-wide and not narrowed).

oneOf.description: The provider org that turned it off here (this org or an ancestor).

OrgModuleState.description: A module's state at one organization.

depth.description: Depth in the tree; the root is 1.

version.description: Optimistic concurrency token. Send it back when updating.

Overlay.description: An integration's overlay: edits by action key.

oneOf.description:
At most this many calls per connection in a window, across every
worker; calls over it wait for the next window.
The body says where the next page is, e.g. `@odata.nextLink`.
The body gives a cursor, sent back as the query parameter `param`.

The query parameter `param` counts items to skip; pages hold
`page_size` items (sent as `limit_param` if given).

Pagination.description:
How a list action pages through its results. Paths are dot-separated
paths in the response body; `items` is where each page's list is
(default: the body itself).

PasskeyAnswer.description: The browser's answer to a passkey sign-in ceremony.

password.description: The user's current password, re-checked before the change.

PayloadField.description: Which half of a step attempt.

via.description: Grants that give it (empty when not allowed).

isRoot.description: The root: the requirement covers every user.

Preference.description: A kind with the user's effective channels.

Preview.description: What an expression gives against a run (the editor's preview).

error.description: Why it couldn't be evaluated, e.g. a name that isn't there.

runId.description: The run it was evaluated against.

Provider.description: A configured identity provider. The client secret is never returned.

ProviderButton.description: A sign-in button: the enabled providers, without configuration details.

redirectUri.description: Register this as the redirect URI at the provider.

ProviderDetail.description: A provider with its role mappings.

ProviderInput.description:
Settings for creating or replacing a provider. Optional fields fall back
to the preset's defaults.

allowedDomains.description: At least one. Only addresses in these domains may sign in.

clientSecret.description: Write-only. Omit on update to keep the stored secret.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, and dashes; appears in sign-in URLs.

name.description: Shown on the sign-in button, e.g. "Microsoft".

PublicForm.description: What someone with the link sees.

Received.description: Only that it was received: nothing about the runs.

recoveryCodes.description: Shown only now. Each code signs in once if the authenticator is lost.
Present when this was the user's first second factor. Shown once.

Rename.description:
An action that seems to have been renamed: gone under one key, back
under another with the same method and path.

oneOf.description: The value set at this org, if any (ignored while an ancestor's lock applies).
Set when an ancestor locked this key: it can't be changed here.
Where `value` comes from; `None` means the built-in default.

value.description: The effective value (`None`: unset, use the documented fallback).

ResolvedSetting.description: A setting's effective value at an org, and why.

ResolvedVariable.description: A variable's effective value at an org, and why.

oneOf.description: Set when an ancestor locked the key: it can't be changed here.

lockedHere.description: Whether this org locks the key for those below.

setHere.description: Whether this org sets the key itself (possibly overridden by a lock).

source.description: Where the effective value is set.

value.description: The effective value; always `null` for secrets.

resumed.description: False unless the run had failed.

retried.description: False if the job wasn't dead (or doesn't exist).

Review.description: What a pack would add, for an admin to approve.

egress.description: Hosts its integrations and HTTP steps call.

installedVersion.description: The version already installed in this organization, if any.

ReviewItem.description: What installing would do to one item.

action.description:
`add`, `update` (installed by this pack before) or `conflict`
(something else has this key: installing is refused).

requireMfa.description: Holders must have a second factor.

key.description:
Lowercase letters, digits, underscores. Derived from the name if omitted
(on create; it never changes afterwards).

RoleMapping.description: A claim value → role at an org.

claimValue.description: The group id, app role, or other value of the provider's role claim.

serviceAccountId.description: An active service account, or null for no identity.

steps.description: Every step that has started, in the order it started.

workflowVersion.description: `null` for a test run of the draft.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens.

revision.description: The revision this edit is based on.

category.description: Where it's shown in the gallery (default "Your templates").

Script.description: A script with its current version.

Server.description: A base URL, possibly with `{variables}` that connections fill in.

options.description: Allowed values, if the spec limits them.

current.description: True for the session making this request.

includeDependencies.description:
When enabling, also enable any modules it requires (default false:
respond 409 listing them instead).

changed.description: Modules whose setting changed, in the order they were applied.

enabled.description: `false` turns it off here and below; `true` removes that.

values.description: Field key → value. `null` clears a value. Other fields are unchanged.

default.description: Used when no org in the chain sets a value.

SettingKind.description: How a setting's value is validated (and edited in the UI).

authorizeUrl.description: Send the browser here; the provider returns it to the callback.

oneOf.description:
With `test`: start at a top-level step, taking the results of the
steps before it from an earlier run of this workflow (and its
inputs, unless `inputs` are given).

test.description:
Run the draft instead of the latest published version (needs
permission to edit the workflow).

next.description: A same-site path to return to afterwards.

state.description:
Bind to the browser (e.g. an `HttpOnly` cookie) and check it equals the
`state` the provider returns before calling `/callback`.

StepRunView.description: The latest attempt of a step.

input.description:
The evaluated input (or a control-flow step's decision); `«redacted»`
when it came from a secret.

stepKey.description: Step id plus loop indices, e.g. `add_member[2]`.

orgId.description: The organization it's for: the form's (default) or one below it.

runs.description: The runs it started, one per workflow with a trigger for the form.

skipped.description:
Workflows that didn't start because the answers don't fit their
inputs (a mismatch between the form and the workflow).

color.description: One of neutral, accent, success, warning, danger, info.

usage.description: How many records carry the tag (that the caller can see).

TaskView.description: A script step attempt's task, as the run page shows it.

logs.description: Its stdout and stderr (scrubbed, at most 64 KiB), once it's done.

assignments.description: The team's role assignments that the caller can see.

TeamMember.description: A member, with enough about the user to display them.

TemplateInfo.description: A template as the gallery shows it.

hasForm.description: Whether using it also creates a form.

orgId.description:
Set for your organization's templates (saved from workflows):
where it lives. Built-ins have none.

otpauthUri.description: `otpauth://` URI to show as a QR code.

secret.description: Base32 secret, for entering into the app by hand.

TriggerView.description: A trigger as the app shows it.

lastError.description: Polls: why the last check failed, if it did.

publicId.description: Webhooks: the path to POST to, `/hooks/{publicId}`.

oneOf.description: Signed by a key this instance trusts.
A valid signature, by a key this instance doesn't trust (yet).

version.description: The version you last read; the update fails with 409 if it changed.

UpdatePreview.description: What importing a newer spec would change, without saving anything.

affected.description:
Published workflows with steps the update would break (among those
the caller can see).

apiVersion.description: The API's own version, from the newer spec.

baseVersion.description: The version this was compared with; pass it when applying.

warnings.description: What the importer worked around in the newer spec.

status.description: `active` or `disabled`. Disabled accounts' tokens stop working.

baseVersion.description:
The version the update was previewed against: if the integration
has moved on since, nothing is applied (409).

status.description: `active` or `disabled`. Disabling signs the user out everywhere.

bindings.description: Values for the template's bindings (missing ones take defaults).

formKey.description:
The new form's key and name, if the template has one (default: the
workflow's key and the template's form name).

key.description: The new workflow's key and name.

emailVerified.description: The user has proved they receive mail at `email`.

kind.description: `human` or `service` (a service account, which uses API tokens).

mfaEnabled.description: Has a second factor (authenticator app) set up.

diagnostics.description: Empty when the document is ready to publish.

locked.description: Stop the organizations under this one changing it.

value.description: A string for `string` and `secret`, a number, a boolean, or any JSON.

Warning.description: Something the importer skipped or guessed, and where.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into the spec, e.g. `/paths/~1users/get`.

diagnostics.description: Problems that would stop the draft being published. Empty when it's ready.

WorkflowDetail.description: A workflow with its draft and the draft's problems.

currentVersion.description: The latest published version, if any.

runAs.description:
The service account that runs started by a schedule, webhook or
event act as. Manual runs act as whoever started them.
